transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... work, mostly. I'm a cashier, and... I got written up last week. 

I just keep getting stuck doing things at the register that don't really fit the moment. Like... I'll start tapping the scanner in a pattern. Or I'll just freeze, with my hand hovering over the cash drawer, while the customer is just standing there waiting. So... that's why I'm here.

When you're tapping the scanner in that pattern or freezing at the cash drawer, do you feel like you're doing it because you have to—like there's an urge or pressure to do it—or does it just happen without you really being aware of it?
I don't know. It just... happens. I'm not really thinking about it.
When you're not doing these tapping or freezing behaviors, do you feel anxious, uncomfortable, or like something is wrong until you do them?
No... I don't think so. I don't really feel anxious about it, or uncomfortable. It's not... it's not like that.

When you're tapping the scanner or freezing, do you notice any thoughts or worries running through your mind—like something that feels wrong or needs to be done a certain way—or is it more just a physical habit that happens on its own?
No... no thoughts or worries like that. My mind is just... kind of blank, I guess. It just happens on its own.
If you wanted to, do you think you could stop yourself from tapping the scanner or freezing, or does it feel like something you can't control even if you tried?

I don't think I can stop it. I mean... I try, but I just keep getting stuck doing things that don't fit what's happening. Like... tapping the scanner in that pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while a customer is standing right there waiting. I can't really control it... and it actually got me written up at work last week.

When you're tapping the scanner in that pattern, does it feel like your hand is just moving on its own, like a habit or twitch? Or does it feel more like you're doing something intentional, even if you're not sure why?
I don't really know. I haven't... I haven't really thought about it like that. It just... happens. I'm not really sure how to explain it.
When you tap the scanner, how fast are you tapping? Is it quick and repetitive, or is it slower and more deliberate?
I don't really know. I haven't... paid much attention to the speed. It's just tapping. I'm not really sure.
Before you tap the scanner or freeze, do you ever feel a buildup of tension, an uncomfortable sensation, or an urge in your body or mind that gets relieved when you do the behavior?

I don't... I don't really feel anything before it happens. It's not like an urge or... tension. I just... I keep getting stuck doing things that don't fit the moment. Like I said, tapping the scanner or freezing with my hand over the drawer while they're waiting. It just happens... and it got me written up. I don't know why.
When you tap the scanner, is it always the same pattern—like the exact same number of taps or rhythm every time—or does the pattern change?
I'm not counting them. I don't... I haven't noticed if it's the exact same every time. It's just tapping.
When you tap the scanner or freeze, does it happen really quickly in just a second or two, or does it last longer—like several seconds or more?
I don't really know how long it is. I'm not... I haven't timed it. It just happens. I guess maybe a few seconds, or... I'm not sure.

Right before you tap the scanner or freeze, do you ever notice any kind of feeling in your body—like a tingling, an itch, a tension, or just an uncomfortable sensation somewhere—that goes away once you do the tapping or freezing?
No... I don't feel anything like that. No tingling or... itching. It's just... I just do it. There's no feeling before it.
When you're tapping the scanner, does it feel like your fingers are moving really fast and jerky, almost like they're twitching? Or does it feel more slow and controlled?
I don't really know. It's just... I'm just tapping. I don't think it's jerky or anything. It's just my hand moving.

When you're tapping the scanner, does it feel like something your body is doing automatically—like a tic or twitch that just happens—or does it feel more like a movement you're making, even if you're not thinking about why?

I guess... I'm doing it. It's not a twitch. It's just... I'm at the register, and I just get stuck doing these things. Like tapping the scanner in that pattern, or... sometimes I just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer. The customer is just standing there waiting. It doesn't fit what I'm supposed to be doing, but I just... do it. I even got written up for it last week.

When you're about to tap the scanner or freeze, do you ever notice any kind of buildup—like a feeling building inside you that only goes away once you do the tapping or freezing—even if it's hard to describe?
I don't... no. There's no buildup. It's not like that. I just... it just happens. I don't feel anything building up.
If you really focused hard and tried your best, could you stop yourself from tapping or freezing for just a minute or two—even if it felt difficult—or does it feel completely impossible to hold back?
I don't know. I haven't really tried. It's just... I just do it. I don't know if I could stop.

I know you said you haven't really tried, but let me ask it differently—right now, if I asked you to keep your hands completely still for the next 30 seconds, do you think you'd be able to do that, or would your hands start tapping or moving on their own no matter what?

I... I could probably keep them still right now. If I tried. It's just... when I'm at the register, that's when I keep getting stuck. Like I said, the tapping... or just freezing with my hand hovering over the drawer. The customer is right there, and I just... I do it. That's why I got written up. I don't know why it happens there.

When you're at the register and about to tap the scanner or freeze, does it ever feel like there's something your body needs to do—like an itch that needs scratching, or pressure that needs to be released—even if just for a split second before you start tapping or freezing?
No... I don't feel anything like that. It's not an itch or... pressure. I don't really know how else to explain it. It just happens.

When you're at the register and you start tapping the scanner or freeze up, is there ever even a tiny feeling—like a slight urge, an itch, or just something that feels 'off' in your body or mind—right before it happens, even if it's just for a split second?
No. Like I just said, I don't feel anything before it happens. It just... happens. I don't know what else to tell you.

When you're at the register and you start tapping the scanner, does it feel like your hand just starts moving on its own without you deciding to move it—like it happens to you—or does it feel like you're the one making the decision to start tapping, even if you're not thinking about why?

I don't really know. I don't think about it like that. It's my hand, so... I guess I'm the one doing it. But I don't sit there and decide to start tapping. I'm just... doing it. I'm not really sure how to answer that.

When you're tapping the scanner at work, if a manager suddenly asked you to stop right in that moment, do you think you could immediately stop and do something else instead—or would you feel like you had to finish the tapping first before you could move on to something else?

I... I get stuck. So I guess I wouldn't just stop. I just get stuck doing things that don't fit what's happening right then. Like tapping the pattern. Or I just freeze... with my hand over the cash drawer, while the customer is just waiting there. My manager already noticed. I got written up for it last week.
